lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: You'll be the new tenant, then. Bait shop's yours till somebody says otherwise.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Rod's on the hook by the door. Your aunt's, it was. Go on, end of the dock.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Hold to cast, let go in the bright bit. Bring me three fish and I'll show you how we do things.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Three fish, love. End of the dock. I'll be right here, pretending not to watch.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Three! And none of them looking at you funny. Good start.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: I'll buy what you catch, right here at the stall. Fair prices. Mostly fair.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Half the village eats what comes off this dock. Lately it's been… thin.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Sell me eight fish. The bigger the better. The odder the better, honestly.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Eight fish for the stall. Bring them here and I'll do the sums.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: That'll feed the Pollards and then some. Here, you've earned a look at the good shelf.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: And the notice board by the stall's got odd jobs, if you want more coin. Folk pay well for strange requests.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: That driftwood stick will snap the first time something with opinions bites.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Harbour Rod. Four hundred and fifty. I'll even throw in some worms.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Harbour Rod's on the good shelf. Four-fifty. I don't haggle. Much.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Now you look like you mean it. Worms are in the tin. Don't open it indoors.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: Look! I drew it before I saw it. That means it's real. That's how it works.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: It's pink and it bites sunsets. It lives near the cove or the Teeth. Catch it? Please?

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: The pink one! Near the cove or the Teeth. It likes sunsets best.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: It looks EXACTLY like my drawing! Except it has fewer legs. I'll fix that.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The light on Gull Point's been dark since the keeper went down. Down, I said. Not away.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: A lamp like that won't take ordinary oil. It wants a light the sea made.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Lampjaw. After the sun's gone. Bring me one.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Lampjaw only shows once the sun's gone. Be patient. The sea is.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: There. Still warm. Hold onto it, it'll want to go home.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Up the stairs, all the way. Put the light where the light goes.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: And when it catches, don't look at the water. Not straight away.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: I'll row you out to Gull Point when you're ready. Just say.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: There she is. Hearthbay's been holding its breath a long while.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: You saw it, didn't you. In the water. Two of them.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Good. Then you're the keeper now. Nobody chooses it. Take the skiff, it was hers.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: She's light on the helm. Push her on and she goes, let her be and she glides. Never cast till she's settled.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: South-west of here there's an isle with a kettle on it. The keeper took her tea there, tides she wanted quiet.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Go and see if it's still warm. It will be. That's the part I don't care for.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Kettle Isle. West of the cove, out past its mouth. You'll know the beach.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Warm, was it. Twelve winters on a bare rock, and warm.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Keep it. Her things go to whoever keeps the light.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: So he's given you the skiff. Good. It's sat at that dock like a held breath.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: South-west there's three black rocks, the Teeth. Deep water. Nothing off them has reached my stall in a long while.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Bring me a Twofold Flounder. And don't let it look at you with both faces at once.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: The Teeth, south-west past the sandbar. Flounder sit deep, so give it line.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Oh, that's the one. Look at it. Looking at us.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: My sister brought these in by the basket. I don't know why I said that. I haven't got a sister.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Tide's kind today. Don't waste it talking to me.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Butterperch fry up lovely. Not that I'd know. I'm far too busy.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: If you see a light out past the Teeth, don't row toward it. Just… don't.

lines.speaker: Mara Thimble
lines.voiceStyle: warm, brisk, middle-aged woman with a soft coastal accent
lines.text: Your rod's older than you are. Treat it gently.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: I'm drawing a fish with nine eyes. No, ten. It keeps changing.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: Biscuit ate my blue crayon. Now everything's a bit green.

lines.speaker: Wick
lines.voiceStyle: excited young child, quick and breathless
lines.text: Did you know fish dream? I asked one. It said yes.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: High water at a quarter past never. Low water just after you've forgotten.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: The lamp remembers. That's the trouble with lamps.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.voiceStyle: very old, slow, gentle man; deep, dry, a little amused
lines.text: Mind the second moon. It minds you.
